results.content: These include data perturbation methods like differential privacy [23], access control, segmentation, and cryptographic techniques such as homomorphic encryption, secure hardware, and secure multiparty computation [24, 25]. #### AI-driven privacy attacks in genomic data security. To address these threats, researchers have explored different privacy-preserving AI techniques to improve genomic data security. As artificial intelligence-driven attacks create immediate privacy concerns, quantum computing introduces long-term risks to genomic data security. By adding AI-resilient defenses and quantum-resistant cryptographic techniques to frameworks like Naveed *et al.’s* and GA4GH standards, a hybrid genomic security model can be created to protect genomic privacy. Future genomic security models should include policy-driven access control, such as the GA4GH Passport Standard, along with quantum-safe encryption to ensure long-term data protection (Section 3.7.2).
